entries.locator: Lecture beat 1: neutrino masses, flavor mixing, energy conservation, and the distinction between prepared and energy eigenstates
entries.note: The opening student question remains the chapter's motivation and is represented as a standalone classroom exchange.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 2: high-barrier symmetric double well and approximate left/right ground states
entries.note: The brick-wall approximation, smooth nodeless one-well ground states, and near degeneracy are preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 3: parity theorem and construction of exact symmetric and antisymmetric states
entries.note: The localized states are explicitly identified as approximate rather than exact energy eigenstates.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 4: overall wavefunction sign, node theorem, tunneling leakage, and exponential level splitting
entries.note: The ground/excited ordering, single central node, and split-energy diagram are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 5: normalized two-state basis and time evolution of an initially left-localized state
entries.note: The phase-sign slip is regularized with the standard e^{-iEt} convention while the board order is preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 6: unit-circle phase picture, complete left-to-right transfer, oscillation period, and energy conservation
entries.note: The condition e^{2 i epsilon t}=-1 and first transfer time pi/(2 epsilon) are derived step by step.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 7: neutrino flavor production, mass-basis propagation, charged-current detection, and long-baseline oscillation
entries.note: Electron and muon production/detection channels and the baseline experiment remain explicit.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 8: questions on epsilon, observation, mass splitting, and experimental status of neutrino mass
entries.note: All four consecutive audience exchanges are retained separately.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 9: ammonia inversion and the distinction between a tunneling barrier and Hamiltonian flavor coupling
entries.note: The NH3 geometry is corrected narrowly while preserving the classroom's chemistry detour and analogy.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 10: spin in a transverse magnetic field as the same two-state mixing algebra
entries.note: The switch from a longitudinal to transverse field, x-basis eigenstates, splitting, and precession are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 11: tau flavor, continuous spin precession, measurement outcomes, and the reason for choosing a weak field
entries.note: The three-flavor extension and both extended spin questions are represented.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 12: minimal-Standard-Model limitation, mass evidence, realistic oscillation refinements, component velocities, and the solar-neutrino deficit
entries.note: The flavor-state language is corrected so that fixed mass components, rather than a classically oscillating mass, carry the phases.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 13: Scientific American claim, electric dipole definition, and dipole versus higher multipoles
entries.note: The deliberate break from formal mathematics and the no-dipole-does-not-imply-sphere argument are preserved.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 14: quantum dumbbell, rotational ground state, and ambiguity of calling a superposition of orientations spherical
entries.note: The J=0 rotational invariance argument is retained without turning it into a classical shape claim.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 15: orientation measurement, angular-momentum uncertainty, rotational energy resolution, and meson comparison
entries.note: The macroscopic dumbbell, molecule, and high-excitation-energy meson examples are all retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 16: boson versus fermion rotational states, electron spin axis, magnetic moment, and the spin-correlated EDM definition
entries.note: The circulating-current picture is labeled heuristic rather than a literal spinning-electron model.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 17: charge quantization question and whether quantum field theory forbids EDMs
entries.note: Both questions are preserved and answered using total charge and symmetry-allowed effective couplings.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 18: parity transformation of polar and axial vectors and the mirror argument forbidding an EDM
entries.note: The board geometry is reconstructed in TikZ and parity violation in weak interactions is retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 19: time reversal of currents, magnetic moments, and charge displacement; antiunitarity and point-particle questions
entries.note: All three classroom questions and the electric-field thought experiment are present.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 20: tiny Standard-Model EDM, null search, new-physics constraints, tabletop context, and audience commentary
entries.note: The null result is presented as support for the Standard Model and a constraint on extensions, not as proof of sphericity.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 21: time reversal versus information conservation, CPT, fixed magnetic fields, and the explicit break
entries.note: The magnetic-field example and need to reverse the external field are kept; CPT is qualified by its standard theorem assumptions.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 22: return to second quantization and the ordinary position/momentum Fourier pair
entries.note: Lower-case wavefunctions, position and momentum probabilities, both transforms, and free-particle plane waves are retained.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 23: continuum field expansion, momentum creation and annihilation operators, inverse transform, and one field per species
entries.note: The garbled ASR stretch is reconstructed from the video, visible board formulas, and standard Fourier normalization.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 24: bosonic mode commutators, local delta commutator, same-point distribution, and Hermitian quadratures
entries.note: Completeness supplies delta(x-y), and the audience question about x=y is retained with a distributional clarification.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 25: noncommuting measurements, separated-point independence, relativistic locality intuition, and EPR correlation versus influence
entries.note: The position/momentum and spin analogies, spacelike-separation argument, and EPR exchange are all present.

entries.locator: Lecture beat 26: fermionic anticommutators, non-observability of odd fermion fields, and next-lecture preview
entries.note: The chapter ends where the lecture ends, with the transition to fermionic second quantization rather than an imposed summary.

entries.locator: Standard physics clarifications
entries.note: Regularizes the Schrodinger phase sign, uses realistic mass-squared oscillation language, corrects NH3 geometry, scopes the minimal Standard Model, treats mass components rather than a classically oscillating mass, labels the current-loop electron picture heuristic, explains antiunitary time reversal and CPT assumptions, reconstructs garbled Fourier formulas, treats delta as a distribution, and distinguishes odd fermion fields from physical even observables. None changes the lecture's argumentative sequence.
